thread:
Julian: Quick heads-up — seeing a TP all-reduce latency spike on the latest runtime build when we scale to 8-way TP. small-message pattern (128B-8KB) looks particularly bad, tail latency up 3-5x vs baseline. :thinking:
Maya: repro steps? which model + workload?
Julian: transformer-60B, TP=8 + PP=1, batch=1, seq=1024 token. Baseline commit 0a1b (last week) vs current 0b2c. Same hardware (A100s), same NCCL version.
Sam: ran micro-profiling this morning. Short summary: ring performs OK for >=32KB per rank, but for fragmented KV updates (~512B-4KB) the ring traversal cost + kernel punch-in dominates. Tree-ish rendezvous or NCCL proto switch helps latency for small msgs.
Sam: pasted raw micro-bench numbers from nsys / ncu:
```
config: TP=8, 8 GPUs (1 GPU per TP rank), all-reduce sum, avg of 50 iters
Message size | ring p50 | ring p95 | tree p50 | tree p95
128 B        | 420 us   | 980 us   | 210 us   | 420 us
512 B        | 480 us   | 1.1 ms   | 240 us   | 520 us
4 KB         | 900 us   | 1.8 ms   | 520 us   | 860 us
32 KB        | 1.5 ms   | 2.1 ms   | 1.6 ms   | 2.4 ms
Observations: ring outperforms tree at >=32KB; tree wins below ~8-16KB.
```
Linh: interesting — matches my theory about traversal overhead vs concurrent pipelining. ring does more serialized H2H hops which amplifies per-message startup for small buffers. We should check NCCL proto (LL vs LL128) + NCCL_ALGO settings. Also check whether our kernel selection is forcing small CUDA kernels that miss occupancy.
Maya: do we see KV cache alignment / fragmentation causing many tiny sends?
Julian: yes — KV cache eviction/flush path creates many 512B reductions when we call prefix-sync for scattered heads. Batching heuristics didn't coalesce because the requests are arriving slightly staggered across TP ranks.
Sam: experiment notes I ran:
- set NCCL_ALGO=TREE + NCCL_PROTO=LL128 -> p95 for 512B dropped ~2x
- set NCCL_ALGO=RING + NCCL_PROTO=LL -> slightly worse for <4KB
- tried aggregation in runtime: coalesced 8 small reduces into one 4KB chunk (local rebuffer) -> p95 reduced by ~40% but increased software latency for first token.
Linh: profiling traces show CPU-side enqueue gaps of ~50-120us between ranks (scheduling jitter) — that prevents aggregation. Might be kernel selection that returns early and schedules small kernels instead of fused kernels.
Sam: attached sample nsys stack snippet:
```
# simplified stack (nsys)
GPU 0  | ncclSend -> cudaLaunchKernel(k_allreduce_small) -> cudaMemcpyAsync(host->dev)
GPU 1  | ncclRecv -> cudaLaunchKernel(k_allreduce_small) -> idle
# lots of kernel setup overhead per message
```
Julian: ops-bot, can you link the perf dashboard traces for the regression? :eyes:
ops-bot: linked -> https://perf.redwood.internal/trace/1881237890 (CI job: tp-allreduce-regress-1881) :white_check_mark:
Maya: action items?
Linh: short-term: enable NCCL_ALGO=TREE for TP paths where expected per-rank message size < 8KB. Add a runtime flag to prefer TREE for small-msg patterns. Also tune NCCL_PROTO to LL128 for medium-small sizes.
Sam: medium-term: improve batching heuristics — introduce a 100us coalesce window per TP rank to gather tiny KV reductions before flushing; add a max-delay config and telemetry so we can detect when coalescing hurts first-token latency.
Julian: long-term: kernel fusion — change kernel selection to prefer fused reduce kernels when we detect high fragmentation (cost model based on msg size distribution). Also investigate protocol-level rendezvous that does hierarchical reduce (intra-node tree, inter-node ring) to get best of both.
Maya: can someone add a small benchmark to perf repo that reproduces 512B scatter reduce and runs both NCCL_ALGO toggles + our coalescing patch?
Sam: I'll add it today and run in CI matrix.
Julian: thanks — please tag me when results posted. Let's try NCCL_ALGO switch + 100us coalesce in a canary and measure p50/p95 across seq lenses 256/1024/2048.
Linh: I'll also dump KV cache eviction patterns into the trace so we can correlate send size histograms with latency spikes.
Sam: FYI the quick script I used to run the microbench:
```bash
# run on 8 GPUs, one process per GPU
mpirun -np 8 -H ... 
export NCCL_ALGO=TREE
export NCCL_PROTO=LL128
python tools/tp_allreduce_microbench.py --msg-sizes 128,512,4096,32768 --iters 50
```
Maya: perfect. ping when CI finishes. :zap:
Julian: resolving for now, leaving thread open for updates. :white_check_mark:
